attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you give your sprite a new name?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you drag the [set sprite to] block inside the [on start] container block?

❓ Did you click the gray box to select a sprite image?

❓ Did you select the Gallery tab from the top menu?
steps.instructions:
Add a sprite to this project, and select an image from the Gallery. This sprite will be the moving sprite. 


Rename the sprite with a simple, descriptive name such as “spaceship”. Click the ⏷ in the red [mySprite] name box to open the drop down menu, then select Rename variable…


Click ▶ to see the sprite appear on the screen!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select the correct sprite name in the [set sprite position to] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja: 

❓Which block sets a sprite’s position?

❓Did you try out different x and y values to move your sprite’s position?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Remind ninjas that sequence matters. Any block that refers to a sprite needs to come after its [set sprite to] block.
steps.instructions:
Set the spaceship sprite’s starting position.


Click the ⏷ on the [mySprite] bubble in the [set sprite position to} block to open the drop down menu, then select the sprite’s name. Then, click in the white bubbles to change the x and y coordinate values.


Click ▶ to see the new position of the sprite.

steps.hints:
❓ Did you click ▶ then use the direction buttons to move your sprite around?


You can also use arrow or WASD keyboard keys to move your sprite:

﻿
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you drag the [move sprite with buttons] block inside the [on start] container block?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Remind ninjas to select the correct sprite name in the new block.
steps.instructions:
Make the spaceship sprite move with the direction buttons on the on-screen MakeCode game controller!


Open the Controller code block menu, and drag in a [move sprite with buttons] event block. Click the ⏷ on the [mySprite] bubble to open the drop down menu, then select the spaceship sprite’s name.


Click ▶ then use the on-screen direction buttons to move the sprite around.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you check if the toggle is set to  “on”?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you drag the [set sprite stay in screen]  block inside the [on start] container block?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Remind ninjas to select the correct sprite name in the new block.
steps.instructions:
Keep the spaceship sprite from moving off the screen!


Open the Sprite code block menu and drag in a [set sprite stay in screen] block. Click the ⏷ on the (mySprite) bubble to open the drop down menu, then select the spaceship sprite’s name.


Click ▶ then use the direction buttons to move the spaceship sprite around, noticing it does not move off the screen anymore.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you set then select the correct sprite name in the [set sprite to] and [set sprite position to] blocks?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which block creates a new sprite?

❓ Which block sets a sprite’s position?

❓ Where should you place the second sprite, so that it is not near the first sprite? 


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Remind ninjas that any block that refers to a sprite needs to come after its [set sprite to] block.
steps.instructions:
Add a second sprite for the spaceship sprite to move towards!


Set and rename the sprite with a simple, descriptive name such as “moon”, then set the sprite’s position on the screen away from the other sprite.


Click ▶ to see the moon sprite appear on the screen, then use the direction buttons to move the spaceship sprite towards it!

steps.hints:
❓After clicking the gray box, did you select the Gallery tab from the top menu?

﻿
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you drag the [set background image] block inside the [on start] container block?

❓ Does the background image show as you intended it to? ❓Will you have to change the position of your sprites so you can see everything clearly?
steps.instructions:
Set a background image for the project!


Open the Scene code block menu and drag a [set background image] block on top of the other blocks inside the [on start] container block. Click on the gray square to select a background image from the gallery.


Click ▶ to see this project’s background appear!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you drag the [set dialog frame to] or [set dialog text color to] block on top  of the [show long text] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you drag the [show long text] block inside the [on start] container block?

❓ Did you use the dropdown menu in the [show long text] block to test out different positions for your dialog box?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Guide ninjas to try out different positions for the dialog text box so it does not block the 2 sprites.

💡The [show long text] should be under the [set sprite to] and the [set sprite position to] blocks.
steps.instructions:
Add a dialog text box to this project, then customize it by adding a dialog frame or changing the text color! 

 

Type a message about this project in the text bubble. Click the ⏷ on the [bottom] value to open the drop down menu, then select a different position for the dialog text box.


Click ▶ to see the dialog text box appear!

steps.hints: 💡The sequence of the code blocks matters. Putting the blocks in a different order will change how the program runs.
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

﻿


Ask the ninja: 

❓Where did you place the screen effect and play sound blocks? Do they work as you expected them to?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Guide the ninja to notice that the order of the code blocks matters. Putting the blocks in a different order will change how the program runs.


💡 Guide ninjas to note that while these customizing blocks are open ended and not required for the game to “work”, they really improve the Player’s experience playing a game, either by giving context to what the Player should do or not do, or to provide a more fun experience overall. They also allow the Ninja to add their personal touch and express themselves through small details present in the game.
steps.instructions:
Add some creative details to this project!


Open the Scene code block menu to drag a [start screen effect] block into this project, then open the Music code block menu to drag a [play sound] block into this project. Allow the sound to play [until done].


Click ▶ to see how these blocks changed this project!

subgroups.introduction: Make a sprite move with the direction buttons on the controller. Then, learn how to keep the sprite from going off screen! Use a background image in the project, too.

validationItems.text: Set the sprite to stay in screen
Use 1 dialog box and set the frame or text color

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of White Belt! In this level, you’ll learn about events, which are actions that trigger code in your project to run. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: An Event to Remember
badges.description: Use events to control actions in a project.

badges.title: Taking Control
badges.description: Use the direction buttons to move a sprite.

badges.title: Think Inside the Box
badges.description: Set a sprite to stay inside the screen.

badges.title: Setting the Scene
badges.description: Add a background image to a project.

badges.title: Layer Cake
badges.description: Use sequence to control which sprite is in front of another.
